document.title: Afghanistan: Al-Qaida Military Contribution to the Taleban
document.authors: Department of State, Bureau of Intelligence and Research (INR)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Newly Published Documents Cast Doubt on Claims Taliban Will Give Up al Qaeda | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret] Two-page INR report on the Taliban's growing reliance on bin Laden and al Qaeda for financial and military support against the Northern Alliance. It covers the 55th (055) Brigade of expatriate mujahideen loyal to bin Laden, estimated at 500-2,500 men. One of two releases of the same report; the earlier one fully redacts the section on camps jointly run by al Qaeda and the Taliban.

key_claims: With reduced Pakistani military aid, the Taleban increasingly rely on bin Laden and al-Qaida for support.
Bin Laden probably contributes several million dollars a year to the Taleban, mostly for military use.
The Taleban could hardly sustain themselves without bin Laden's supply of foreign volunteers.
The 55th Brigade is composed mostly of expatriate mujahidin loyal to bin Laden and used as shock troops, with 500-2,500 members.
Almost all Afghan training camps are associated with both al-Qaida and the Taleban, with joint training in poisons, sniping and explosives.
